# Trusted validation repair brief

Extend #167's merged report plumbing so a failed issue/PR validation yields coordinator-owned repair evidence and a useful status summary. No automatic repair loop or harness changes.

**Shape: Involved.** Classification spans validation execution, persisted trusted artifacts, workflow resumption and two status commands; retain one report model rather than adding a parallel evidence store.

## What we know
- `internal/workflow/engine.go:91,1086` already carries `ValidationReport` in `WorkResult`; `internal/pr/service.go` propagates it to PR results. Preserve #167's behavior and tests.
- `internal/validation/validator.go:40,57,270` defines check/report data and trusted artifacts; `check_diagnostics.go` already bounds FAIL blocks and names. Its name list lacks package identity, so it cannot safely drive package-specific reruns alone.
- `validator.go:101,165,396` loads base policy/config and executes through `checkRunner`; `build_cache.go` already provides approved-base snapshot execution machinery. Reuse these boundaries, environment and timeout controls.
- `engine.go:939` currently directs repair to VALIDATION.md. `import_policy.go:25` already restricts developer active outputs to IMPLEMENTATION.md and LESSONS.md; keep that allowlist.
- `internal/workspace/ci_evidence.go:38-81` normalizes and quotes untrusted diagnostics. `fingerprint.go` and validator metadata support serialized validation evidence; status must read coordinator-recorded evidence, never local agent files.
- All modification targets below exist in this supplied snapshot. There is no repository Git metadata here (`git status` fails), so approved-base tree membership cannot be independently verified in this planner sandbox.

## Assumptions and open questions
- Snapshot contents represent the approved base. Cheapest confirmation: coordinator/implementer checks each path with `git cat-file -e <approved-base>:<path>` before implementation. No source file is designated new in this plan; extend existing files. The required fragment `changes/unreleased/190-trusted-repair-brief.md` is absent in this snapshot; **absence at the approved base remains unconfirmed** and must be checked there (reuse an existing issue fragment if present).
- A test not observed executing on base (new test/package, build failure, timeout, unsupported command, truncated/ambiguous identity) cannot honestly receive one of the three classifications. Record an unavailable reason and require human diagnosis; never count it as pre-existing. Implementation fixtures will settle package attribution and subtest selection. No inaccessible environment blocks implementation.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints
1. **Structured evidence and classification:** extend `internal/validation/{validator.go,check_diagnostics.go,go_fastpass.go,build_cache.go,fingerprint.go}`. Add additive per-test package/name/classification and bounded rerun evidence to the existing report, retaining current failing_tests/output_tail fields. Capture package identity from Go test events or reliably delimited package output; do not infer it from the changed-package list or replay output as shell code. Preserve bounded streaming capture, including plain-text FAIL blocks and non-Go tail fallback. Record changed packages using existing Go discovery, with an unavailable explanation if discovery fails.
2. After a failed Go check, select only its failing package/test pairs. Build anchored, regexp-escaped per-subtest selectors, safely quote arguments, retain trusted relevant build/test flags, and disable test caching (`-count=1`). Run each selection once on candidate and at approved base through the same checkRunner boundary/config and clean environment; reuse approved-base snapshot/cache setup and clean it up on every exit. Candidate passes => flaky; candidate still fails and base test executes/passes => regression; same test executes/fails on base => pre-existing. Missing tests, compiler errors and infrastructure failures remain unclassified. Do not run the full suite for classification, treat discovery output as authority, or let candidate caches poison base execution. Keep overall validation failed even for flaky evidence. Bound cumulative diagnosis time/output and propagate cancellation/claim expiry.
3. **Trusted projection:** render REPAIR.md from that report inside validation (reuse CI escaping/quoting pattern without creating a validation/workspace import cycle); root-bound atomic safefs writes only. Include checks, names/classifications, bounded FAIL blocks/tails, changed files/packages and base/head identity. Persist the structured report in existing trusted validation artifact metadata on failures as well as successes, through existing fenced RecordTrustedValidation calls. Validate identity before reuse. Never reconstruct authority from tester prose or REPAIR.md. Extend existing `internal/workspace/advance_base.go` stale-evidence cleanup for REPAIR.md. Clear stale brief on success/base/head change; rebuild on resumption from current trusted evidence. A cached passing report must not resurrect an old failure brief.
4. **Workflow and callers:** extend `internal/workflow/engine.go` to regenerate the brief before a repair developer invocation and reference REPAIR.md as untrusted diagnostic data. Before invoking developer, stop when every failed outcome/test is conclusively pre-existing; mixed, non-Go or unclassified failures must not take this shortcut. Return a typed workflow error carrying the trusted result; map it in `internal/cli/next_action.go` to human_required with no automatic retry. Apply on immediate failure and resumed issue/PR work. Preserve import rejection, approval and claim checks; do not edit protected developer prompt templates. Inspect existing validation callers in `internal/pr/service.go`, `internal/cli/{validate.go,work.go,submit.go,work_validation.go,output.go}` so additional report fields survive existing error/result paths. Rebase conflict repair remains out of scope.
5. **Status:** extend `internal/cli/{status.go,pr.go,validate.go,next_action.go}` and `internal/pr/service.go` to expose the same structured summary in issue/PR status text and JSON from current trusted artifact evidence. Share decoding/rendering with report plumbing rather than parsing Markdown. Reject mismatched base/head evidence; legacy absent/malformed summaries show unavailable without crashing. Status must not execute reruns.
6. **Tests/docs:** extend the existing tests listed in TEST_PLAN.md; explain the brief, classifications and maintainer stop in existing `docs/developer.md` and `docs/WORKFLOWS.md`; add the issue changelog fragment after the base existence check. No new flags/config or protected paths. Developer writes only source, tests, docs/changelog, IMPLEMENTATION.md and LESSONS.md; any other active-bundle edit rejects the entire run.

## Verification and scope
Run build, changed-package vet, then targeted tests before the single full `make check` run. The implementation should fit one 16-hour claim budget. Base-tree existence verification is a coordinator review item because this planning snapshot has no Git database; do not silently assert it passed.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Planner: keep the plan compact; build on #167's merged validation report plumbing in WorkResult. List the existing tests, docs and call sites your change affects, and confirm every file you call new is absent at the base. The developer writes only source, tests, docs, IMPLEMENTATION.md and LESSONS.md; changing any other file under .swarm/active/ discards the whole run. Run go build ./... and go vet on changed packages, then targeted tests; at most one full suite.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
